questions.question: Which statement is the core assignment invariant?
options: Every nearby driver marker is available for assignment
Every trip event must be consumed globally before a driver is assigned
A trip has one authoritative version and at most one assigned driver at a time
The pricing multiplier owns the trip state
questions.explanation: Location, scores, and consumers may be stale or replayed, but only one versioned trip transition can own the driver assignment.

questions.question: Before spatial-cell overhead, what candidate scoring rate comes from 1,200 rider requests per minute and 40 candidates per request?
options: 48 candidate scores per second
800 candidate scores per second
20,000 candidate scores per second
48,000 candidate scores per second
questions.explanation: 1,200 requests per minute is 20 requests per second; 20 multiplied by 40 candidates is 800 candidate scores per second.

questions.question: Why can both very small and very large geospatial cells be expensive?
options: Both always reduce the number of fresh drivers
Both require a global transaction for every GPS update
Both force the matching radius to zero
Small cells multiply index lookups, while large cells scan more false candidates
questions.explanation: The useful operating point balances cell fan-out against false-candidate filtering rather than maximizing or minimizing cell size blindly.

questions.question: What should dispatch do with a driver coordinate outside its freshness bound?
options: Offer the trip and refresh the coordinate after acceptance
Exclude the candidate, then expand or return a longer honest wait under policy
Treat the last coordinate as exact until the trip completes
Move trip authority into the location index
questions.explanation: Retrying stale evidence does not make it fresh. A stale driver is not valid matching capacity.

questions.question: During a peer-region partition, which design best protects an active trip?
options: Let both regions accept trip transitions and reconcile later
Pause every trip in every region
Keep one fenced home-region writer and queue peer replication for reconciliation
Delete local event history so the peer can start cleanly
questions.explanation: Local ownership keeps one trip history. Replication freshness can degrade without creating a second writer.

questions.question: Dispatch times out after an assignment may have committed. What is the safest next action?
options: Replay or read using the same idempotency key and expected trip version
Create a new trip ID and send the offer to another driver
Publish an assignment event before checking trip state
Assume timeout means the transaction failed
questions.explanation: The same command identity lets trip authority return the committed result or apply one legal transition without duplicating side effects.

questions.question: Which dispatch metric reveals that riders will become progressively staler even if current request latency still looks acceptable?
options: Average driver rating
Number of pricing experiments
Total historical trips
Age and growth rate of the oldest queued match request
questions.explanation: Queue age and growth expose accumulating work. A short latency sample can hide requests waiting behind an expanding backlog.
